This is a complaint instituted under Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (hereinafter referred to as 'FSS Act') for violation of section 3/26/27 punishable under section 59 of FSS Act.

2. Brief facts leading to filing of the present complaint are that on 14.02.2020 at about 02.30 pm,
Sh. Kuldeep Singh Suman, Food Safety Officer (FSO) along with Sh. Naubat Singh visited the premises of M/s Symphony Banquets - A Unit of Multiple Hospitality and disclosed his identity to the Food Business Operator (FBO) Sh. Pradeep Kumar, who was conducting the business of the food articles including 'Paneer'.

After inspection of the premises, complainant showed his intention of purchasing a sample of 'Paneer' for analysis, where the said food article was stored in an open tray bearing no label declaration for ready for use for the preparation of Paneer Tikka, Shahi Paneer &
other dishes of Paneer which were intended for human consumption, to which he agreed.

The complainant tried to associate some public witnesses by requesting passersby but when none came forward, then complainant requested to Sh. Naubat Singh, Field Assistant, for witnessing the proceedings to which he agreed and joined as witness in the sample proceedings.

Thereafter, the complainant purchased a sample of 'Paneer' for analysis from FBO Sh. Pradeep Kumar and price of the sample was disclosed by the FBO to be Rs. 236/- which was offered to the FBO in cash but the same was not accepted by him as sample was not for direct sale.
3. Thereafter, the sample consisted of approx. 1 kg of 'Paneer' taken after cutting it into smallest possible pieces with the help of a clean and dry knife provided by FBO in a clean and dry tray.

The same was mixed properly with the help of clean and dry steel spoon provided by FBO by rotating it Food Safety Officer vs Pradeep Kumar And Ors on 11 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174035877/
2 in all possible directions several times.
The sample of aforesaid food article divided in to four counterparts then and there by putting it equally in four clean and dry glass bottles with the help of same spoon.
Thereafter, 20 drops of formalin added in each counter part of sample with the help of a clean and dry dropper.

Each glass bottle containing the sample was separately marked, packed,
fastened and sealed according to the provisions of the Food Safety and standard Act, 2006 and Rules & Regulations made thereunder.

The signature of the FBO were obtained on the Designated Officer's slip bearing signature of the then Designated Officer Sh. Bal Mukund and also on the wrapper of the bottles containing the sample, in such a manner that the same was partly visible on the then Designated Officer slip and partly on the wrapper of the sample bottles.
The complainant also obtained signatures of the FBO on the labels of all counter parts of the sample.
Notice in Form VA was prepared at the spot and copy of the same was given to FBO.
A copy of this notice was also served to supplier, M/s S. S. Paneer World.
The Food Business Operator did not request to send the fourth counterpart of the sample for analysis from an NABL accredited Laboratory under Rule 2.4.5 of The Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011.
The Panchnama and Raid report was also prepared at the spot.
All the sampled documents prepared by the complainant were read over and explained to FBO in Hindi, who signed the same after understanding the same.
These documents were also signed by the complainant himself and by the witness Sh. Naubat Singh, Field Assistant.

4. Thereafter, one counter part of the aforesaid sample of 'Paneer' bearing sample No.
747/1051/22/2020 and the then Designated Officer Code No. 07/DO-26/15250 was sent to the Food Analyst, Govt. of NCT of Delhi for analysis on 17.02.2020.
The FBO did not request to send the fourth counterpart of the sample for analysis from an NABL accredited Laboratory under Rule 2.4.5 of The Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011.

The remaining two counterparts of the sample along with two forms VI in a sealed packet as well as the fourth counterpart of the sample along with one form VI in a separate sealed packet were deposited to the then Designated Officer Sh. Bal Mukund on 17.02.2020.

The Food Analyst in his report No. FSS/290/2020 dated 20.02.2020 has opined,
"The sample is substandard because moisture exceeds the prescribed maximum limit of 60.0%."

The then Designated Officer of District West, Sh. Bal Mukund sent a copy of the intimation letter along with analysis report of Food Analyst to the FBO on 21.02.2020 for giving them an opportunity to file an appeal against the report of the Food Analyst under section 46(4) of the FSS Act, 2006 for sending one part of the sample to the Referral Food Laboratory.

The FBO preferred an appeal against the report of Food Analyst under rule 2.4.6 (1) of The Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011 before the Designated Officer of District West Sh. R. K. Bhaskar on 12.03.2020 and one counterpart of sample was sent to the Director, Referral Food Laboratory, Ghaziabad (U.P.) on 13.03.2020.
5.

The Director, Referral Food Laboratory, Ghaziabad vide certificate No. 191/Apr/20-ND dated 16.04.2020 has opined, "The sample of Paneer does not conform to the standards laid down under Regulation no. 2.1.16 of Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additive)
Regulation, 2011, as the sample shows the presence of B.R. Reading above the maximum prescribed limit, indicating the presence of foreign fat.

6. It is further averred that M/s Symphony Banquets- A Unit of Multiple Hospitalityis a partnership firm having two partners namely, Sh. Suhel Nagpal and Sh. Jagdish Lal Nagpal.

However, said firm has appointed Sh. Pradeep Kumar as nominee under FSS Rules, 2011 and at the time of sampling,
he was looking after the day to day conduct of its business, therefore, he was responsible for conducting day to day business and as such in-charge of and liable for offence.
It is further alleged that M/s Multiple Hospitality being a partnership firm was also liable for offence.
It is further alleged that the above said food article 'Paneer' was manufactured by M/s S. S. Paneer World and supplied to M/s Symphony Banquets.

It is also alleged that M/s S. S. Paneer World is a proprietorship firm and Sh. Sarvagya Sujan is the proprietor of said firm and looks after the day to day business of the firm and as such he is in-charge of and responsible for the conduct of its business and liable for the offence.

It is further alleged that the above mentioned accused violated the provisions of Section 26(1) and 26(2) (i) read with Sections 3(1)(zz)(iv) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 & also violated Regulation No. 2.1.16 of the Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011.

After conclusion of the investigation, the case containing the statutory documents and Food Analyst report, was sent by Sh.

Bhaskar, Designated Officer, District West to the Commissioner (Food Safety), Department of Food Safety, Government of NCT of Delhi, who accorded the consent under Section 42(4) of the FSS Act, 2006 for the prosecution of accused in exercise of the power vested in him under section 30(2)(e) of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and directed the complainant to institute the prosecution.

sentences.text: Upon filing of the present complaint, cognizance was taken vide order dated 11.02.2021.
Upon service of summons, appearance was entered by accused No.1 who also represented accused No.2.
However, accused No.3 was not served with the summons as he had already expired and vide order dated 26.03.2022, proceedings against the accused No.3 stood abated.

After complying with the provision under section 207 Cr.P.C, vide order dated 02.07.2022, notice for the offences under section 3/26/27/59 of FSS Act was served upon the accused No.1 to which he pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
Thereafter, the case was fixed for prosecution evidence.
8. The prosecution examined FSO Sh. Kuldeep Singh as PW1.

He deposed on the lines of the complaint and relied upon the following documents:
(a) FBO receipt Ex. PW1/A,
(b) Form VA Ex. PW1/B,

Accordingly, the prosecution evidence was closed on 12.02.2025.

Thereafter, statement of the accused under section 313 Cr.P.C was recorded in which the accused No.1 stated that he was innocent as the food article was supplied by accused No.3.
10.
Final arguments heard.
11. The case of the prosecution is that the sample of the food article i.e. Paneer lifted from the premises of the FBO/accused No. 1 and supplied by accused No. 3 (since deceased) was substandard.
The prosecution itself has founded its case that the food article was supplied by accused No. 3 (since deceased).

The FSO has obtained the documents Ex.PW1/M-1(colly) including Food Safety Officer vs Pradeep Kumar And Ors on 11 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/174035877/

sentences.text: The FSO has admitted in his cross-examination that there was no dispute raised by accused No. 3 (since deceased) about the identity of the commodity supplied.
Since, the accused No. 1 and 2 were not the manufacturer of the food article, they are entitled to the benefit of warranty u/s 27(2) of FSS Act.

It was held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in P. Unnikrishnan Vs. Food Inspector, Palghat Municipality, Kerala, 1996 2 PFAC 25, that the supplier was entitled to benefit of warranty u/s 19(2) of PFA for a food article manufactured and supplied by the manufacturer firm.

entities.text: P. Unnikrishnan Vs. Food Inspector, Palghat Municipality, Kerala, 1996 2 PFAC 25
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, the accused No. 2 is duly licenced firm.
Hence, accused No. 1 and 2 are entitled for warranty.
12. The report of RFL has categorized the food article as substandard since B. R. reading of the sample was below the minimum prescribed limit.

As per the report, the B. R. reading of the extracted fat was 39.1 at 400 C. The FSS (Food Products Standards and Food Additives)
Regulations, 2011 do not provide for any standard for any extracted edible fat.

Reliance is placed on the judgment of Prakash Chand Vs. State of M. P., 1993 I PFAC 28.
13.

sentences.text: In view of the above, prosecution has failed to prove its case against accused No. 1 and 2 for the violations of Section 3/26/27/59 FSS Act.
Therefore, accused No. 1 and 2 stand acquitted of the charges u/s 3/26/27/59 FSS Act.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Since, the accused No. 1 and 2 were not the manufacturer of the food article, they are entitled to the benefit of warranty u/s 27(2) of FSS Act.
It was held by Hon'ble Supreme Court in P. Unnikrishnan Vs. Food Inspector, Palghat Municipality, Kerala, 1996 2 PFAC 25, that the supplier was entitled to benefit of warranty u/s 19(2) of PFA for a food article manufactured and supplied by the manufacturer firm.
In the present case, the accused No. 2 is duly licenced firm.
Hence, accused No. 1 and 2 are entitled for warranty.
12. The report of RFL has categorized the food article as substandard since B. R. reading of the sample was below the minimum prescribed limit.
As per the report, the B. R. reading of the extracted fat was 39.1 at 400 C. The FSS (Food Products Standards and Food Additives)
Regulations, 2011 do not provide for any standard for any extracted edible fat.
Reliance is placed on the judgment of Prakash Chand Vs. State of M. P., 1993 I PFAC 28.
13.
In view of the above, prosecution has failed to prove its case against accused No. 1 and 2 for the violations of Section 3/26/27/59 FSS Act.
